Gandhism may be well suited to a society which does not accept democracy as its ideal. questions.questionText: W.V.O. Quine, in his paper, "Two Dogmas of Empiricism", rejects the boundary between synthetic and analytic statements. Which among the following correctly depict(s) his proposal of 'Empiricism without the Dogmas'?

contentBlocks.content: W.V.O. Quine, in his paper, "Two Dogmas of Empiricism", rejects the boundary between synthetic and analytic statements. Which among the following correctly depict(s) his proposal of 'Empiricism without the Dogmas'?

options: Science is like a field of force where experience constitutes the boundary conditions
Re-evaluation of some statements entails re-evaluation of others, because of their logical interconnections
Any statement can be held true come what may, if we make drastic enough adjustments elsewhere in the system
No statement is immune to revision except the logical laws
